messages:
Mia Chen: Heads up — AtlasPay on Dedicated reported a bursty perf regression tied to their batch formation. p95 token latency jumped ~40% after we switched kernels last week.
Ryan Patel: :eyes: Do we have a repro? dataset + config from AtlasPay?
Mia Chen: They sent a profile. Looks like KV prefetch thrash — a lot of small queries that blow up batch token estimates and then we overshoot the token budget.
Sanjay Iyer: That aligns with what the profiler showed: `kernel_v2` increased copy stalls for short-seq requests. Continuous batching heuristics end up grouping too many short requests because estimated token weights are stale.
Eva Gómez: Can we tune the queue policy for their Dedicated pool? AtlasPay asked for explicit token budget and queue limits to avoid tail latency.
Mia Chen: Proposed minimal config to test:
```yaml
dedicated_pool: atlaspay-prod
batching:
  max_queue_depth: 48
  token_budget_target: 1600   # target tokens per formed batch
  per_request_token_cap: 512
  short_seq_threshold: 64
  short_seq_weight: 0.6
  prefetch_suppression_window_ms: 15
```
Mia Chen: The idea is suppressing aggressive KV prefetch for bursts and lowering effective weight for short seqs so they don't bloat batches.
Ryan Patel: I like adding `per_request_token_cap` — should prevent single long requests from stealing budget. How did you pick 1600?
Mia Chen: From their p50/p95 seq distribution in the upload. 1600 keeps avg batch size ~8-12 requests, which we saw was optimal in staging.
Sanjay Iyer: Also add a queue policy rule: prioritize older requests if queue depth > 32 so we don't starve high-latency items. Example: `if depth>32 then reorder by enqueue_ts asc`
Eva Gómez: AtlasPay explicitly asked for queue-level ceilings: "no more than 64 queued requests and max tokens queued 32k" — will that conflict?
Mia Chen: We should map that to our budgeting: `max_queue_depth: 48` + `global_token_queue_cap: 32768`. Keeps headroom while respecting their ask.
Sam (ops): infra-bot created a canary for atlaspay-prod yesterday: deploy id `deploy-6b9f`, running kernel_v2 with config from staging. Logs: `batch_form_time_ms` spikes correlate with short-seq bursts.
Ryan Patel: If kernel_v2 copy stalls are the root cause, we can try a kernel selection override for AtlasPay to `kernel_v1` for their pool as a quick mitigation. Any downside?
Sanjay Iyer: v1 is slightly less memory efficient but lower latency for short sequences — should be fine for a canary. We can do an automated rollback if throughput drops.
Mia Chen: Plan: 1) apply proposed batching config + global token queue cap, 2) override kernel to v1 for atlaspay-prod canary, 3) monitor p50/p95 tokens and KV hit/miss rate.
Eva Gómez: I'll draft the customer-facing reply: explain the short-term rollback to kernel_v1 and the config changes, promise metrics in 2 hours.
Mia Chen: I'll push the config to the canary and open a short dashboard: `atlaspay/dedicated/batching/canary-v2` with these panels: batch_size, p95_token_latency, kv_prefetch_rate, queued_tokens.
Sam (ops): Done — config push scheduled in 5m. infra-bot will post status.
infra-bot: deploy started `deploy-6b9f` -> atlaspay-prod | kernel: v1 | batching: atlaspay-canary-0319
Ryan Patel: After 30m, if p95 drops back near baseline we'll roll to full pool. If not, escalate to perf sprint.
Mia Chen: Agreed. Will post observed numbers. :thumbsup:
Eva Gómez: cc @account-team — sending customer note now.
Mia Chen: (follow-up) initial canary after 8m: p95 token latency down 28%, queued_tokens peak down 40%, kv_prefetch_rate down 65%. Uploading screenshots to the thread.
Ryan Patel: Great. Keep the canary running for another 1h and then promote. Thanks team.
